articles.title: Re-Grading the Biggest NHL Offseason Trades and Signings 1 Month Into the 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: It's kind of wild to think about all the time we had during the NHL offseason for trades and signings to settle out, and how quickly everyone got thrown into the fire of a new season.
articles.body:
It's kind of wild to think about all the time we had during the NHL offseason for trades and signings to settle out, and how quickly everyone got thrown into the fire of a new season.

And now that season is a month old, and we've got an appetizer of those players in new locations, which gives us plenty of early ammo to judge how they've done.

We recognize how difficult it can be to adjust to a new team, and we'll do our best not to be too harsh, but the play can force the issue, good or bad. It's not quite a report card, so don't sweat showing it to your parents, but just know we're watching closely anyway.

JJ Peterka's arrival in Boston via trade with Utah got him back on the East Coast and playing for fellow German head coach Marco Sturm. That combination of elements, as well as Peterka providing speed and skill to the Bruins lineup, is paying off early on.

Through 12 games, Peterka has four goals and five assists, and while David Pastrňák leads the team in scoring by far with 17 points, Peterka is part of a mass of Boston players supporting him in a big way. After getting beaten by Buffalo in the first round of the playoffs last year due in part to not being as fast as them, Peterka adds that to Boston's lineup without altering the way the team plays.

Peterka's scored 25-plus goals in three straight seasons, and with the style of game he's got and the way the Bruins are playing in general, it's not wrong to think that Peterka could crack 30 goals for the first time in his career (he's on pace for 27).

It's been a very average start to the season for the Blues. Literally.

They're 5-5-1 and in the middle of the pack in the NHL. That said, one of the reasons they've been successful this season is the summertime trade acquisition of Mason McTavish.

McTavish is tied for the team lead in scoring with Dylan Holloway, with 10 points, and his six goals are tied for the team lead with Jimmy Snuggerud. McTavish's no-quit style and up-tempo play have been an ideal fit for the Blues in their new lineup.

His advanced stats are middle of the road but not negative, and if you're hoping for sustainability, those are good signs. That he's on pace for around 45 goals should have Blues fans beyond excited.

There's a lot to like about what Pavel Dorofeyev has shown with the Rangers, but there are causes for concern just the same.

In 14 games, Dorofeyev has three goals and five assists, a pace of 18 goals and 47 points. After signing him to a seven-year, $77 million deal this summer after acquiring his rights from Vegas, that outcome would be a brutal start to his Blueshirts career.

Of course, Dorofeyev is a shooter, and shooters can be streaky. Right now, he's in a cold spell. He's shooting 7.1 percent this season, and coming into this season, his career average was 14.8 percent. Generally, players don't stay cold all season, so things are bound to turn around.

On the flip side, Dorofeyev's bad luck might also mean poor defensive results when he's on the ice, too. His plus-minus rating is minus-13, which ties him with Patrick Kane for the lowest mark in the NHL. We know plus-minus is not a catch-all stat, but when it's a mark that's tied for worst in the league, there's no amount of spinning you can do to make it look better. It's just bad.

The offense will rebound eventually, and the defensive numbers should improve with them. At least the Rangers hope they will.

When Alex Tuch and the Buffalo Sabres couldn't come to terms on keeping the Syracuse-area native in Western New York, the Capitals were more than happy to add him, knowing full well that Alex Ovechkin didn't have many more years left to play.

Right now, it looks like they were geniuses, even if they did pay a high price.

Tuch's eight-year, $84 million deal in a sign-and-trade with Buffalo has provided the Capitals with nine points in 10 games (tying him with Dylan Strome for the team lead) as well as a team-leading seven goals. His skills have been a natural fit in Washington and have helped the Caps out to a 6-4-0 start, including a 5-2-0 home record.

Tuch has teamed up on a line with Strome and fellow newcomer Jordan Kyrou, and if that's how they're going to start the season, maintaining that success will be vital to getting Washington back to the playoffs and being Eastern Conference contenders.

Florida adding Brady Tkachuk to their roster to join his brother, Matthew, was always going to be a high-profile move and ripe for scrutiny if it didn't work out.

Apart from the tough showing in Ottawa on Brady's return to face his former team, things have gone very well for him with the Panthers.

Brady leads the Panthers with seven goals, and he's tied for second on the Panthers in scoring with Seth Jones with 12 points, trailing only his brother with 16 points. Brady not needing to be a captain in Florida and just focusing on playing hockey is working out quite well for him, and it's benefiting the Panthers.

Florida is right in the mix in the middle of everything in the Atlantic Division and Eastern Conference, while going without Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand, as well as missing goalie Jacob Markström for a spell. Adding Brady to the mix was always going to be a bit of a luxury, but for now it's playing out a little better than expected.

Part of how the Utah Mammoth wanted to build on making the playoffs a year ago was to add more experience and veteran leadership to their extremely talented young core. The easiest way they did that was to add Vincent Trocheck from the New York Rangers.

Trocheck's value to the Mammoth won't necessarily be measured through points and goals, although they do help. His role with Utah is to take on that responsibility to win draws (63.1 percent) and give scorers like Logan Cooley and Dylan Guenther someone to defend strongly on their line.

Trocheck is helping his line maintain the puck and generate shots (56.5 CorsiFor%) as well as facilitating high-quality chances at 5-on-5 (62.8 xGF%). With three goals and four assists in 12 games, on top of the strong advanced numbers, he's off to a very good start while playing a much larger role.

When Bowen Byram let the Buffalo Sabres know he wasn't interested in signing an extension there and was ready to move on to be a No. 1 defenseman elsewhere, the Chicago Blackhawks were more than eager to make that happen.

Chicago took Byram and Jordan Greenway from Buffalo in exchange for the No. 4 pick in the draft, a second-round pick, and Louis Crevier, and then signed Byram to a six-year, $75 million extension to keep him from becoming a free agent. With hopes being sky-high for a turnaround, things could not be going worse for the Blackhawks and Byram.

In six games, Byram has no goals and one assist and has a plus-minus of minus-7. Although his advanced stats are among the best on his team, they're not very good in either shots (45.4 CorsiFor%) or shot quality (40.5 xGF%) at 5-on-5. Meanwhile, the 'Hawks are 3-8-0 to start the season, and there have been little to no signs of improvement even after Connor Bedard's return from injury.

It's early in Byram's Chicago career, and you have to hope this is as tough as it'll be.

When the Panthers brought Jacob Markström back to Florida in a trade with New Jersey to replace Sergei Bobrovsky, the hope was that the veteran would get his mojo back where his career began. The bar Bobrovsky set last season was low to clear, although his legacy with two Stanley Cups also makes it impossibly difficult.

Although Markström is dealing with an injury now, the start of his reunion with Florida has been decent enough. He's 3-1-1 in six games with an .897 save percentage and a shutout. It helps to note that the current league average is .892 for context.

His 2.21 goals-against average is solid, and while the Panthers have had other serious injuries interrupt their aim to return to glory, the play that Markström has provided has given them reason to feel positive about where things can go.

It's easy to forget Markström has had seasons where he was among the best goalies in the league, and once/if the Panthers get back to good health, having him near the top of his game will give them the chance to be in the mix for the Cup again.

During the offseason, one of the biggest shopping list items for the San Jose Sharks was to add experienced defensemen to help push them further up the standings and back into the postseason.

Arguably, their biggest addition was Darnell Nurse in a trade with Edmonton.

The move to add Nurse had more detractors than it did supporters, but with the way the Sharks play, a defensive defenseman like Nurse (and Jacob Trouba) was seen as a natural fit.

Through 11 games, Nurse has a goal and an assist while playing just over 21 minutes a night. Unfortunately, the Sharks are allowing 3.5 goals per game while scoring 3.0 themselves, and that raises concerns about both the goaltending and the defense. In Nurse's case, his 5-on-5 advanced stats are deeply worrying.

Nurse's shot metrics (38.8 CorsiFor%) as well as shot quality (36.0 xGF%) are the worst on the team among regulars. A defenseman playing the kind of minutes he does and spending most of the time seeing tons of shots against and struggling to deny quality opportunities is a major contributing factor to the Sharks' goals-against problem.

Better goaltending may help stop some of the goals, but when the defense is allowing so many opportunities, it's an issue that goes deeper.

When the St. Louis Blues moved Jordan Kyrou to Washington in an offseason trade, it gave him the opportunity to start fresh after a couple of difficult seasons.

Teaming up with another new Capitals forward is working out well for Kyrou and the team all the same.

In 10 games, the 28-year-old has two goals and six assists (eight points), and he's been able to give the Capitals a dynamic second line with Alex Tuch and Dylan Strome.

While Tuch leads the team in goals, Kyrou running and gunning with him and Strome is proving to be difficult for opposing teams to contain, especially when the Caps are at home, where they're 5-2-0.

Although Kyrou was more of a goal scorer with the Blues, those opportunities should come with Washington. His eight points are tied for third on the team with Ryan Leonard, just one behind linemates Tuch and Strome.

When Sergei Bobrovsky and the Florida Panthers weren't able to work something out, where he landed in free agency was a bit of a mystery. Seeing him land with the Toronto Maple Leafs as part of their massive offseason makeover was somewhat surprising. So far, whatever expectations could be had for his performance have been met...depending on your point of view.

If the hope was to see the Bobrovsky who took over in the postseason for the Panthers and was a world beater, then there's disappointment to be had. If the player we've seen during the regular season the past few years was who you thought you'd see, then you're looking like the smartest person in the room.

Bobrovsky's 3-4-2 record with an .897 save percentage and 3.02 goals-against average is just above league average. Although backup Anthony Stolarz has better save percentage numbers (.907 SV%; 2.79 GAA), the lead job is Bobrovsky's, but the dual setup and the reemergence of Auston Matthews have the Leafs off to a strong start. If Bob can play steady and get Toronto back to the playoffs, the hope of seeing "Playoff Bob" is enough to give the Leafs reason to believe.

Patrick Kane's return to Chicago was celebrated by many Blackhawks fans, and his two-year, $16 million deal to come back and, ideally, help be the veteran guide for a young team to get back to the playoffs was something the player and team were enthusiastic about.

On the one hand, Kane leads Chicago in scoring with seven points (one goal, six assists) in 11 games. On the other, he's tied with Rangers forward Pavel Dorofeyev for the NHL's lowest plus-minus rating at minus-13.

Chicago went without Connor Bedard for the start of the season, so Kane leading them in points so early may not be too big of a surprise. That it's with just seven points while the 'Hawks average 2.18 goals per game is a team-wide concern.

Chicago wasn't signing Kane to compete for the Selke Trophy, but his struggles extend beyond a poor plus-minus rating: His five-on-five numbers are also concerning (39.2 CF%; 36.9 xGF%).

With team-wide numbers suffering similarly, the issues are well beyond what Kane is doing (or isn't).

articles.title: El régimen iraní ahorca a un alpinista y crece la preocupación por el destino de más deportistas
articles.standfirst: La organización de ex deportistas iraníes Human Rights for Sport, con sede en Oslo, asegura que ya han sido ejecutados seis en casos vinculados a las protestas antigubernamentales
articles.summary: La organización de ex deportistas iraníes Human Rights for Sport, con sede en Oslo, asegura que ya han sido ejecutados seis en casos vinculados a las protestas antigubernamentales
articles.body: el alpinista Ali-Sina Mostafavi ha sido asesinado por el régimen iraní. No ha sido el primer deportista ni será el último que paga con su vida el simple hecho de oponerse a un Gobierno que lleva años cometiendo todo tipo de atrocidades contra su propia población. Mostafavi no era un deportista profesional al uso pero dejó constancia gráfica de sus ascensos a algunas de las cumbres más altas del mundo, incluido el Everest. Fue ejecutado el pasado 14 de octubre tras haber sido arrestado en abril. Su 'delito' fue participar en las protestas antigubernamentales ocurridas a principios de enero de 2026, en las que murieron más de 3.000 personas. Su muerte se suma a la del taekwondista Siavash Jamshidi Kheirabadi a principios de octubre y del luchador de artes marciales mixtas Gholamreza Khani Shakarab, quien fue ahorcado en mayo. Pero como advertíamos, la ejecución de Mostafavi puede no ser la última. De hecho, la organización Human Rights for Sport, con sede en Oslo e integrada por un grupo de exdeportistas iraníes, ha advertido que al menos seis deportistas más pueden ser ejecutados después de que el Tribunal Supremo de Irán confirmara sus sentencias. Entre ellos se encuentran el nadador Ali Pishevarzadeh y el futbolista Ehsan Hosseinpour, ambos arrestados durante las protestas de enero, y Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani, un boxeador arrestado en 2020 por participar en protestas un año antes. Su solicitud de un nuevo juicio fue rechazada el año pasado. Otro luchador de MMA, Benyamin Naghdi, la amazona Taraneh Rahimi y la escaladora Maryam Siri también han sido condenados a muerte este mismo año. Sus nombres se pueden sumar a la de seis deportistas que ya han sido ejecutados por casos vinculados a las protestas de enero o a cargos políticos anteriores. “La comunidad deportiva iraní está bajo una enorme presión. En el caso de uno de los condenados a muerte, logramos llamar la atención y sensibilizar a través de otras organizaciones, y consiguieron que se detuviera su ejecución. Pero fue solo temporal y estoy muy preocupada por todos ellos”, aseguró Zohreh Abdollahkhani, miembro de Human Rights for Sport, en declaraciones a The Guardian. Esta organización asegura que los deportistas han sido blanco de ataques para enviar un mensaje a la sociedad en general, y que las muertes de deportistas destacados suelen recibir una amplia cobertura en los medios estatales. Entre ellos se encuentra Navid Afkari Sangari, un afamado luchador que fue ejecutado en septiembre de 2020. “Era un modelo a seguir y muy conocido en toda la comunidad. Lo que le sucedió también fue una advertencia para toda la población: miren lo que podemos hacerle a alguien así”, dijo Abdollahkhani. En el caso de Mostafavi, fue acusado de ser un "agente armado del enemigo sionista estadounidense" y arrestado por presuntamente abrir fuego contra civiles en la plaza Azadi de Kerman el 24 de marzo y participar en las protestas de enero. Human Rights for Sport constató que 217 deportistas iraníes fueron asesinados a tiros en enero y más de 100 fueron detenidos. Cuatro miembros del Parlamento Europeo también escribieron a la FIFA antes del pasado Mundial para expresar su preocupación por los estos deportistas iraníes que se enfrentaban a la ejecución, pero Abdollahkhani afirmó que no recibieron respuesta. “La FIFA es consciente de las preocupaciones suscitadas en relación con la situación de los deportistas iraníes y agradece a todas las partes involucradas su continua colaboración y dedicación para concienciar sobre estos asuntos cruciales”, fue lo que declaró un portavoz del organismo rector del fútbol mundial. Abdollahkhani también criticó al Comité Olímpico Internacional (COI) por dificultar la presentación de denuncias en su departamento de derechos humanos pero éste se defendió asegurando que contaba con "equipos de derechos humanos y protección plenamente operativos", añadiendo que, como organización no gubernamental, carecía de autoridad para modificar las leyes o el sistema político de un país soberano.

images.caption: El alpinista Ali-Sina Mostafavi durante una de sus ascensiones. Ali-Sina Mostafavi/Iran Human Rights

articles.title: Week 8 Fantasy Football Waiver Wire: Rookies Jonah Coleman, Omar Cooper Jr. headline top pickups
articles.summary: Justin Boone gives you his recommendations off the waiver wire at each position for fantasy football in Week 8.
articles.body:
Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

Roster percentages are generated from Yahoo leagues. Free-Agent Budget (FAB) amounts are based on a $100 salary cap. Only players rostered in less than 50% of leagues are considered.

The Dolphins earned their first victory of the season on Sunday and Willis had his second straight quality fantasy performance — sandwiched around Miami's bye.

After finishing as the QB13 in Week 5, Willis was the QB4 overall this week. That result is thanks to a three-touchdown day (two passing, one rushing), as well as 208 yards through the air and another 37 on the ground. He's now run the ball at least eight times in three of his last four appearances.

The most exciting development for Willis has been the emergence of his skill position talent with Caleb Douglas, Malik Washington, Chris Bell, Greg Dulcich and Ollie Gordon II stepping up in recent weeks.

While the Patriots make for a tough test, Willis will have a much softer stretch versus the Lions, Colts, Bills and Jets again coming up after that. With his rushing upside giving him a solid fantasy floor, Willis will be a streaming option every week and now we're seeing the ceiling to go along with that in better matchups.

Kirk Cousins is 57% rostered but would be the No. 1 QB add, if available.

Risky streaming options (if starter is out)

There's a reason why I haven't stopped highlighting Coleman in this column all season. In his first game back off injured reserve, the rookie immediately led the Broncos' backfield in what is now a three-man committee.

Coleman played nearly half the snaps, while RJ Harvey and J.K. Dobbins shared the other half. Coleman also led the team in scrimmage yards (69), touches (11) and routes run (11). Unfortunately, it was Harvey who scored a long touchdown and Dobbins who took a goal-line carry into the end zone.

Don't be misled by the final fantasy points though, Coleman's usage is what matters here. Sean Payton expressed a very clear desire after the game to get the fourth-rounder even more touches moving forward.

Though the ceiling might be partially limited at the moment with Harvey and Dobbins still involved, fantasy managers need to be aggressive anytime there is a potential starting back available on the waiver wire.

The Broncos have one of the five easiest fantasy schedules for RBs the rest of the way. Hopefully you took my advice and stashed Coleman, but even if you didn't there's still an opportunity to add him in 65% of leagues. I'm valuing Coleman as a possible low-end RB2 with upside.

Black is another rookie backup I've been featuring in this column all season, encouraging managers to stash him away in case of a Christian McCaffrey injury.

The veteran did get banged up on Sunday, but was fortunately able to return to the game in the second half. That led to increased usage for Black, who rushed 12 times for 63 yards and a score. It was his highest output since a 15-touch, 70-yard stat line in the opener.

McCaffrey downplayed the quad injury after the game and with a bye week to rest up, I'd expect him back at full health in Week 9. However, it's clear that Black is up to the challenge if his number is ever called.

Stashing a talented No. 2 back playing behind a 30-year-old starter who handled 450 touches last season isn't the worst idea in the world. Black should be rostered everywhere and would provide RB2 fantasy production with RB1 upside if McCaffrey ever missed time.

The trade rumors surrounding Jonathan Taylor seem like more than just speculation at this point. The Colts are also facing another very tough matchup against the division rival Jaguars in Week 8.

That might be why McGowan earned his biggest snap share of the season on Sunday (34.5%). It would be smart for Shane Steichen and company to get a look at what the seventh-round rookie can offer in a large role.

To McGowan's credit, he's performed well on his limited touches this year, including his season-high 48 yards against a stout Vikings' front in Week 7. With news of a Taylor trade potentially being announced at any moment between now and the Nov. 10 deadline, it's wise to stash McGowan on your bench until then. Let's just hope that Indy doesn't get a starting-caliber running back as part of the return in a JT trade. The Colts have one of the 10 best fantasy RB schedules in the second half of the season, so McGowan could be a sneaky fantasy option down the stretch and it won't cost you much to get him now.

Knight's value will evaporate the moment that Jeremiyah Love returns to the lineup. But if the rookie remains sidelined in Week 8, Knight will be an intriguing fantasy option against a generous Cowboys defense.

Over the last two weeks, Knight has been the more productive back in Arizona, racking up 161 scrimmage yards on 27 touches. Tyler Allgeier has only managed 97 yards on 30 touches. This will all come down to Love's availability, so don't go overboard trying to acquire Knight. He's just a spot starter if Love continues to sit out.

This is an extreme long shot, but Conner is a potential trade candidate who's sitting on IR in Arizona. I have the veteran stashed in several leagues, just in case the Cardinals send him to an RB-needy roster before the deadline.

Rachaad White is 55% rostered but would be the No. 2 RB add behind Coleman, if available.

Best one-injury away backup RBs to stash

Mike Washington Jr. at NYJ (30% rostered)

Chris Rodriguez Jr. vs. IND (24% rostered)

Dart-throw flex options (if starter is out)

Cooper led this column last week and here we are again with him still barely coming in under the 50% rostered cutoff.

Even with Adonai Mitchell back in the lineup for Week 7, Cooper continued to shine with his second straight 100-yard outing. The rookie has now finished as a top-10 fantasy WR in back-to-back games with stat lines of 6-103-1 and 5-115-1. It also makes you wonder if he would have threatened the 100-yard mark in his debut, since he posted 30 yards on just five snaps before getting hurt.

After spending a month on IR, the first-round wideout looks like the real deal and has more favorable matchups on the way with the Raiders (Week 8), Bills (Week 10) and Dolphins again (Week 12). He was a must-add last week and now he's an "empty the waiver wire budget to get him" kind of pickup. Cooper is a high-end WR3 with a much bigger ceiling, which he has put on display the past two games.

Normally, I just list Tyson as a one-line sentence below, since he's rostered in almost 50% of leagues. However, his return is nearing and that rostered percentage isn't moving.

This is another talented first-round receiver who was dominating Saints' practices this summer before suffering another hamstring injury. It's hard to ignore almost everyone around the organization praising his skills and suggesting he would be a star at some point this season.

In Kellen Moore's fast-paced offense, there is plenty of room for another productive pass-catcher alongside Chris Olave… just ask Devaughn Vele.

It's not hyperbole to say that Tyson could be a major factor in fantasy leagues in the second half of the season when the Saints return from their Week 8 bye. You should have already stashed him in your IR spot, but if you didn't you can still solve that problem and get yourself a potential WR3 with WR2 upside once he's healthy.

With DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks out of the lineup, Lemon had his best game yet with seven catches, 67 yards and a touchdown on eight targets against the Cowboys. We always knew Lemon was more of a long-term play, since he was a rookie who missed significant practice time in the summer due to injuries. So, it's great to see the first-round pick finally producing in what's been a chaotic season for the Eagles.

With speculation that Smith could miss more action due to his hamstring injury and no timeline on Wicks' return, Lemon is a must-add if he's still on the waiver wire in your league. He's a fantasy WR3/flex with the usual upside that comes with first-year players in the second-half of their debut campaign.

One of the most important things for first-year players to show in their early NFL action is that they belong on the field with the pros. While every player is different, when a rookie hits the ground running it's an obvious indicator of future success. When they're able to look comfortable and be productive, we have signals for stardom.

Douglas has managed to accomplish both those feats in his limited time on the field. After breaking onto the scene with a five-catch, 94-yard effort in Week 1, Douglas suffered an ankle injury that sidelined him for a month.

Coming off the bye, he picked up where he left off with 70 yards and a pair of touchdown catches.

While I'm not viewing Douglas in the same light as Cooper or Tyson, the third-rounder still has weekly WR3/flex potential and should be added in most leagues.

The Jaguars are returning from bye after a Week 6 outing where Hunter and Meyers were extremely productive.

Hunter only played nine offensive snaps, but was the first-read on many of those plays which led to four catches, 59 yards and a touchdown. With Brian Thomas Jr. getting fewer snaps and potentially going to be traded, Hunter's offensive involvement could rise. As we witnessed in his last game, it doesn't take much for Hunter to make an impact in real life and fantasy. Few players offer the kind of ceiling Hunter possesses, so he's an important stash.

Meanwhile, Meyers is a weekly WR3/flex option with double digit fantasy points in three of his six appearances this season. That includes a season-high 10 targets and 83 yards before the bye. Though I prefer chasing Hunter's ceiling, Meyers is the more proven fantasy option.

Terry McLaurin is done for the season, which opens the door for Williams to emerge as a consistent weapon in the Commanders offense.

The third-round rookie actually led Washington's receivers in snaps and routes run in the loss to the 49ers, finishing the game with 50 yards on three receptions. We've also seen him flash multiple times in the first six weeks, including a four-catch, 64-yard, one-touchdown debut and an 87-yard TD in Week 4 that was called back due to a penalty.

With all the attention on bigger names, Williams is sliding under the radar a bit as he returns from the Commanders' bye week. Make no mistake, Williams has WR3/flex potential with McLaurin out for the remainder of the season.

In deeper formats, you can also consider his teammate Treylon Burks, who stepped up in McLaurin's absence with four catches and 66 yards. He's also scored a pair of touchdowns this season. However, he walked off late in their last game with trainers, so we'll need to make sure he's healthy.

Brian Thomas Jr., Jaguars (trade candidate)

Thomas' rostered percentage has fallen far enough for me to include him in this column. This one is simple though, you stash him now and wait to see if he gets traded before the deadline.

A fresh start on a receiver-needy team could do wonders for the former first-rounder who put up 87 catches, 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns in 2024. Doesn't that seem like a lifetime ago, considering how the last two seasons have unfolded for BTJ?

KC Concepcion is 60% rostered but would be the No. 3 WR add behind Cooper and Tyson, if available.

Tre Tucker is 58% rostered but would be the No. 6 WR add behind Cooper, Tyson, Concepcion, Douglas and Hunter, if available.

Terry McLaurin's injury also frees up more targets for Okonkwo, who is finally back to playing a normal snap share after missing time with a hamstring injury in the opening month.

Over his last two games before the bye, Okonkwo put up 60 yards on six targets versus the Giants and 69 yards on seven targets against the 49ers.

Prior to the arrival of Stefon Diggs, Okonkwo was one of my favorite sleepers this summer. With McLaurin sidelined, the 27-year-old tight end is once again set up to challenge for low-end fantasy TE1 value rest of season.

This isn't Strange's first appearance in this space, but he continues to be disrespected by fantasy managers. The 25-year-old is a high-end TE2 streamer with low-end TE1 potential.

Strange is averaging the sixth-most targets among tight ends over the last month and has at least seven targets in each of his outings during that span. He's also posted three very usable stat lines of 7-95-0, 7-68-0 and 5-44-0. That includes two top-12 weekly fantasy finishes.

While many non-elite tight ends have fantasy success due to touchdown-scoring, Strange is earning the kind of volume that could make his production more sustainable. Given his role in one of the best offenses in the league, Strange needs to be rostered, especially in a week with George Kittle and Isaiah Likely on bye.

Hunter Henry is 56% rostered but would be the No. 1 TE add, if available.

T.J. Hockenson is 53% rostered but would be the No. 2 TE add behind Henry, if available.

Darnell Washington vs. CLE (3% rostered)

Cam Little is 56% rostered but would be the No. 1 K add, if available.

Quarterbacks: Aaron Rodgers, Justin Herbert

Running Backs: Tyler Allgeier, MarShawn Lloyd, Kendre Miller

Wide Receivers: Xavier Worthy, Josh Downs, Chris Godwin Jr., Wan'Dale Robinson

Tyler Allgeier was expected to be the main beneficiary if first-round rookie Jeremiyah Love got hurt, but that's not how it has played out. Over the last two weeks with Love sidelined, Allgeier has split work with Bam Knight, with Knight being the more productive option. That led to Knight playing more snaps in Week 7. If Allgeier doesn't have one-injury away upside, then he doesn't need to be rostered.

When Josh Downs posted back-to-back 70-plus yard games in Week 2 and Week 3, it appeared he might have a chance to unlock a new ceiling the rest of the way with Alec Pierce sidelined. Unfortunately, he's failed to reach 50 yards in any game since and has settled into the low-ceiling flex territory for fantasy.

We all knew wideout Jordyn Tyson would eventually return and erase Juwan Johnson's fantasy upside, but Johnson didn't even wait for the rookie to get back in the lineup. The veteran has disappeared from the fantasy radar, while being limited to stat lines of 4-16-0, 0-0-0 and 1-7-0 the last three weeks. Now he's heading on bye and Tyson might be activated after that.

Mark Andrews hasn't topped 50 yards in a game this year and has been held under 30 yards in each of the past four weeks. The veteran is just a TD-or-bust fantasy TE2, who only has one score on the season.

articles.title: Historic 5th Inning And Much More: Brewers' World Series Game 3 By The Numbers
articles.summary: Here are the numbers to know from the Milwaukee Brewers' blowout win over the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 3 of the 2026 World Series.
articles.body: The Milwaukee Brewers squeaked past the Tampa Bay Rays in Games 1 and 2 of the 2026 World Series. But, in Game 3, the Brewers got past the Rays with a sledgehammer. After earning a 10-1 win in Tampa Bay, the Brewers now have a 3-0 series lead and are on the verge of their first World Series triumph following a historic Game 3 rout and a dramatic, eight-run fifth inning. Here are the numbers to know from Game 3 of the 2026 World Series with nuggets provided by FOX Sports Research: 0: The number of outs Rays reliever Cam Booser recorded in relief of starter Freddy Peralta in the top of the fifth inning; Booser, who entered the night having surrendered zero runs over six innings pitched this postseason, gave up four consecutive hits and was pulled. 1A: Brewers manager Pat Murphy challenged an inning-ending force-out in the fifth. He won the challenge, and Milwaukee went on to drive in eight runs on six consecutive hits. The Brewers are the first team to log seven consecutive hits in a postseason game. 1B: The aforementioned inning also tied the 1921 New York Giants (Game 3) and 2001 Arizona Diamondbacks (Game 6) for the most runs scored in a World Series game without hitting a home run. 2A: The number of baserunners (one hit and one walk) Brewers starting pitcher Robert Gasser surrendered over six scoreless innings. 2B: Ironically, the Brewers only scored in two innings, plating two runs in the third and eight in the fifth. 3A: The number of hits the Rays were held to; designated hitter Yandy Díaz had two of those hits. 3B: Milwaukee had three players tally three-plus hits: Jackson Chourio (four), William Contreras (three) and Brice Turang (three). 4A: Chourio's four hits came throughout the first five innings, making him the fourth player to do so in a World Series game. Moreover, Chourio became the youngest player (22 years and 229 days old) to have four hits in a World Series game since Joe Garagiola had four hits against the Boston Red Sox in Game 4 of the 1946 World Series. 4B: The number of baserunners (three hits and one walk) the Brewers' pitching staff held the Rays to. 5: Peralta surrendered a combined two runs across his first three starts and four appearances altogether this postseason (16 ⅔ innings). Then, the Rays' right-hander entered the fifth inning of Game 3 with two earned runs to his name in the outing and went on to be credited for five earned runs. 6: Gasser became just the second pitcher to face the minimum number of batters through six-plus innings in a World Series game; Don Larsen's perfect game in Game 5 of the 1956 World Series for the New York Yankees is the only other performance. 8A: On the eight-inning front, the Brewers became the first team in MLB history to score eight runs with two outs in a World Series game. The Los Angeles Dodgers are the only other team to score as many runs with two outs in a playoff game, bringing home 10 runs with two outs in the first inning of Game 3 of the 2020 National League Championship Series against the Atlanta Braves. 8B: Eight of Milwaukee's nine starting position players recorded a hit. 8C: Eight different players drove in a run for the Brewers. 16: The number of hits Milwaukee had. 26: Milwaukee's pitching staff recorded 26 outs before giving up a run. articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s $2 billion fortune puts Lionel Messi on a 2027 countdown to join football’s most exclusive financial club
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has become the first active athlete to pass $2 billion in career earnings, according to Forbes' latest ranking.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo has become the first active athlete to pass $2 billion in career earnings, according to Forbes' latest ranking. The 41-year-old forward sits at an estimated $2.09 billion, ahead of golfer Tiger Woods at $1.97 billion and Lionel Messi at $1.87 billion. His contract with Saudi club Al Nassr pays him more than $200 million a year. Forbes projects his total will reach about $2.39 billion by May 2027, while Messi, 39, is expected to cross the $2 billion line by the end of next year. Ronaldo is also 18 goals short of 1,000 in club and international football.Cristiano Ronaldo passes $2 billion in career earningsThe Al Nassr deal does most of the heavy lifting now, but it is not the whole story. Ronaldo has recorded at least $100 million in estimated annual earnings for 10 straight seasons, a run that covers his time at Manchester United, Juventus and Real Madrid as well as Saudi Arabia. Few athletes hold their market price that long. Most see it fade once the legs slow down.That consistency is the number worth noticing. One big transfer can inflate a single year. Ten in a row points to a brand that works whatever the club.The headline figure needs a caveat, though. Career earnings are not net worth. Forbes counts salary, bonuses and endorsements, and it does not adjust for taxes, agent fees or inflation. On the net worth side, Forbes puts Ronaldo at $1.2 billion. He made its billionaire list for the first time in June, edging Messi, who is estimated at $1.1 billion. The gap between what he has earned and what he keeps is wide, which is normal at this level.Then there is the football side. The 1,000-goal chase is a marketing gift. Sponsors like a countdown, and Ronaldo has one running.Messi and the NBA stars are closing inMessi is third on the list, about $220 million behind Ronaldo. At 39, he is projected to reach $2.02 billion by the end of 2027, helped by an estimated $145 million in income this year. That income is tied to his move to Inter Miami and reported revenue-sharing arrangements with Adidas and Apple TV.Even so, the yearly gap is clear. Al Nassr alone pays Ronaldo over $200 million, while Messi's all-in figure sits well below that.His route looks different from Ronaldo's. After leaving Paris Saint-Germain in 2023, Messi reportedly turned down a $400 million-a-year offer from Saudi Arabia and signed with Inter Miami instead. The club's valuation has since climbed to $1.35 billion, the highest in MLS. He also holds an option to buy an equity stake once he retires, and he already owns pieces of Spanish clubs CD Eldense and UE Cornella. Ronaldo's money is salary-led. Messi's is drifting toward ownership, and that may matter more once the boots are off.Woods sits second at $1.97 billion, roughly $120 million back, so Ronaldo's lead over him is slimmer than over Messi.Basketball has its own billion-dollar names now. Stephen Curry and Kevin Durant both crossed $1 billion in career earnings during the 2025-26 NBA season, according to Forbes. Curry is at about $1.02 billion and Durant at roughly $1.06 billion.On Forbes' numbers, the gap between the two stars probably grows in the short term. Ronaldo is projected to add about $300 million by May 2027. Messi needs until the end of that year to add roughly $150 million.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Former WWE stars CJ Perry and Rusev expecting their first child together after navigating an emotional IVF journey
articles.summary: Former WWE stars CJ Perry, popularly known as Lana, and her husband Rusev are expecting their first child together after an emotional in vitro
articles.body: Former WWE stars CJ Perry, popularly known as Lana, and her husband Rusev are expecting their first child together after an emotional in vitro fertilization (IVF) journey. The couple's pregnancy announcement marks a major milestone in their personal lives after they reconciled to start a family.Perry and Rusev got engaged in 2016. Before their engagement, the two had been paired on screen but not romantically. In fact, at the time of the engagement, they had actually been featured as a team on-screen.It is to be noted that the couple got married on July 29, 2016, sharing much of their relationship both on television and through social media. However, they separated without filing for a divorce. This did not last long, as the couple reconciled after renewing their wedding vows in a private Los Angeles church ceremony in early 2025.CJ Perry, aka Lana and Rusev are planning to welcome their first child, couple shares their IVF journeyFormer WWE star and wrestling couple CJ Perry and Rusev, also known as Lana and Miro, are planning to welcome their first child after their marriage in 2016. The couple has been candid about their fertility journey, with both stars previously discussing the challenges and hopes associated with IVF.CJ Perry also took to her Instagram account to share the news with their fans, stating, “We are pregnant! It’s been such a journey. We are so so grateful."Perry first revealed that they were undergoing the treatment during an appearance on Daria & Toni Unwrapped in November 2025. Speaking to People, Perry revealed that she’s pregnant with a baby boy and is currently due on April 28, 2027. Reflecting on her IVF journey, she shared that the couple started IVF back in 2025 before finally reaching the embryo-transfer stage this past August. Perry said their embryo transfer took place on August 10, and then came nine very long days before they could even take the first pregnancy test.“We started IVF in 2025, and on August 10, 2026, we had our embryo transfer. We were so nervous. We had to wait nine days for our first pregnancy test on August 19, followed by another on August 21 to confirm the pregnancy.” She even added, those days were very tough for both of them. Those days felt like the longest of our lives! There was a lot of surrendering, letting go, and trusting God through the uncertainty," Perry added.She even stated that hearing their son’s heartbeat for the first time really drove home what they had been through to get there. “The first time we heard his heartbeat, I couldn’t stop giggling. I was so full of gratitude and joy. We’ve been blessed with such a miracle.”Rusev, who returned to WWE in April 2025 after his stint with AEW, has also spoken publicly about the couple’s plans to become parents. In February 2026, he discussed their IVF journey during an appearance on Chris Van Vliet’s Insight podcast and shared some of his ideas for their future children’s names as well, dropping hints to his fans that the couple was planning to start a family soon.The announcement reflects their deeply personal journey as a couple who struggled and faced several challenges. It also highlights a new chapter beyond their professional wrestling careers as they prepare to welcome their first child together.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How Sean Payton made Broncos' offense worse after taking over play-calling duties
articles.summary: The Denver offense has regressed in a key area since Sean Payton took over again.
articles.body:
Early in the 2026 season, the Denver Broncos made a huge change to their offense: Sean Payton took play-calling duties back from Davis Webb.

The offense was really struggling to get anything going early this season, and Payton felt a change was needed. Well, the Broncos made the switch in Week 5, and they're 3-0 since then. But that doesn't tell the full story.

As ESPN's Jeff Legwold highlighted, the Broncos offense has actually regressed in one very important phase of the game: third downs. Payton's version of this offense is worse on third downs than Webb's, as they're struggling to convert all kinds of third downs.

Broncos' third-down production has gotten worse since Sean Payton took over

"Since coach Sean Payton took back playcalling duties in Week 5, the offense has gotten worse on third down," Legwold writes. "Denver was 4-26 (15.4%) on third down in the two games combined before Sunday."

Payton's first two games didn't go well on third down, and even in their Week 7 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals , the Broncos went just 3-of-11 on third down.

Denver went 2-of-12 in Week 1, 4-of-11 in Week 2, 7-of-13 in Week 3, and 8-of-17 in Week 4 on third downs with Webb as the play-caller.

Overall, the Denver offense went 21-of-53 on third down with Webb calling the plays in Weeks 1 through 4 (39.6%), and in three games with Payton as the play-caller, the Broncos offense has gone 7-of-37 (18.9%) on third down.

The Broncos have clearly regressed since Payton took over, with their third-down conversions with Payton being more than twice as worse as it was under Webb.

That's made worse by the context that Webb's version of the offense faced the Kansas City Chiefs , Jacksonville Jaguars , Los Angeles Rams , and San Francisco 49ers , while Payton's faced the Los Angeles Chargers , Seattle Seahawks , and Cardinals.

While the Seahawks are the most challenging defense on that schedule, the Cardinals and Chargers are two of the worst defenses in the NFL. For Payton's offense to struggle that much on third down against them is a bad sign.

While the Broncos' win-loss record looks better with Payton calling the plays again, this important third-down statistic shows the offense has taken a noteworthy step back since he took over play-calling duties in Week 5.

articles.title: Raiders cut 3rd-year starting defensive tackle
articles.summary: To make room for the activation of WR Dont'e Thornton from IR, the Raiders made a surprise cut of a regular starting DT the past couple season.
articles.body:
It would appear DT Jonah Laulu has fallen out of favor with the Raiders this season. After appearing in every game his first two seasons in Las Vegas and starting 22 of those games, he was waived Tuesday.

The move was made in correspondence with WR Dont'e Thornton being activated from injured reserve. But it's telling that, with a somewhat crowded group of interior defensive linemen, that is was Laulu who got the ax.

Twice this season Laulu has been placed on the inactive list, including this past Sunday against the Rams . The move was made clearly for the purposes of trying to bulk up to stop the Rams' run game. A plan that failed miserably with their top two backs both nearly putting up 100-yard games.

Also inactive for the game was Thomas Booker IV. Those moves were made in favor of second-year sixth round pick. JJ Pegues and undrafted practice squad call up Tim Keenan.

Pegues in particular has spent four of the team's seven games this season on the inactive list. And he forced a fumble in Sunday's game along with putting up a couple tackles.

It could be simply that the team figures Laulu is the most likely to go unclaimed so they can re-sign him to the practice squad. We will see both if that holds true this time tomorrow when he will either be claimed or clear waivers and is eligible to be re-signed.

articles.title: Flyers’ Jacob Gaucher & Cam York Back on the Roster
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Flyers executed a few key roster moves ahead tonight’s matchup against the Columbus Blue Jackets, headlined by defensemen Cam York from inju...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Flyers executed a few key roster moves ahead tonight's matchup against the Columbus Blue Jackets, headlined by defensemen Cam York from injured reserve and the recall of forward Jacob Gaucher.

Cam York Returns to Stabilize the Blue Line

After missing eight games with an upper-body injury, top-four defensemen Cam York has officially been activated off injury reserve.

The 25-year-old blueliner, who averaged over 21 minutes of ice time per game prior to his injury, is expected to return immediately to provide a much needed boost to Philadelphia's defense. During York's absence, the team suffered a 3-4-1 record.

The Flyers placed veteran defensemen Rasmus Ristolainen on injured reserve Monday, clearing a spot for York on the roster. Ristolainen suffered an upper-body injury and is expected to be out for roughly two weeks.

The Flyers officially recalled center Jacob Gaucher from their AHL affiliate, the Lehigh Valley Phantoms on Tuesday.

Gaucher was reassigned to the Phantoms on Sunday, marking a quick turnaround back to the NHL. The 25-year-old forward gives head coach Rick Tocchet flexibility down the middle as the team struggles to stay out of the Metropolitan Division basement.

The Flyers head into tonight's matchup with a record of 3-7-3, marking them seventh in the Metropolitan Division. With York back on the ice and Gaucher back on the roster, the Flyers look to string together momentum as they face division rivals in back-to-back games, starting with Columbus at the Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia tonight at 7 p.m. EST.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson injury update: Ian Rapoport reports Ravens’ star QB will play Week 8
articles.summary: When will Lamar Jackson return from his ankle injury?
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has missed the last three games due to a high ankle injury. The Ravens desperately need him back after two straight losses. The Cincinnati Bengals crushed the Ravens 35-17 in Week 7. The Bengals scored 35 unanswered points.

Tyler Huntley did a commendable job as Jackson's backup, but the offense just isn't the same without the two-time MVP.

Jackson had thrown for 967 yards and four touchdowns before he got hurt in Week 4. ESPN NFL Insider Ian Rapoport 's reporting raised questions about when Jackson might return to the lineup.

Here's when the QB could be under center for Baltimore.

Will Lamar Jackson start in Week 8 against the Buffalo Bills?

Ian Rapoport is reporting that Jackson should be ready to start in Week 8 against the Buffalo Bills . The NFL insider went into detail about his injury and said:

"First of all, I expect, based on the people I've spoken with, that Lamar Jackson will play this week. He will be on the field this week against the Buffalo Bills. I know he's been here before. This is a two- to three-week injury. He is,through the third week, he is believed to be as close to 100% as he has been. And the Ravens do expect him to play, and based on the people I'm talking with, I expect him to play as well."

Jackson didn't agree with Rapoport's original reporting about his ankle injury. He clarified that it was a high ankle injury. It will be an epic QB matchup with Josh Allen this Sunday. Allen has been great so far this season. The Bills are 5-1-0, and Allen has been a touchdown machine. He has recorded nine passing TDs and eight rushing TDs. articles.title: Wildcat Wrap: Arizona men’s golf tested against top competition at East Lake Cup
articles.summary: Editor’s note: With several sports going on, Wildcat Wrap serves as a recap that focuses on the Arizona programs that we do not have the time to cover on a r...
articles.body:
Editor's note: With several sports going on, Wildcat Wrap serves as a recap that focuses on the Arizona programs that we do not have the time to cover on a regular basis but are certainly worthy of recognition.

Fresh off one of the best postseason runs in program history, the Arizona men's golf program is getting a test of where it stands against top-ranked teams at this week's East Lake Cup in Atlanta, Georgia.

Arizona finished fourth of out of four teams in the stroke play portion of the tournament. The Wildcats shot one-over par, behind Auburn (13-under), Oklahoma State (11-under) and UCLA (8-under).

The four programs were the semifinalists in last year's NCAA Championships. Arizona fell to UCLA in the national semifinal match. Auburn went on to beat UCLA for the national title.

Tianyi Xiong led Arizona Monday in stroke play with a 2-under to finish sixth individually.

On Tuesday, Arizona fell to Auburn in match play by a score of 4-1. The lone point came from Xiong. Auburn is the No. 3 team in the nation. Arizona entered the tournament unranked.

In addition to Xiong, Arizona's starting lineup incudes returners William Wistrand and Matej Baca . Arizona has two newcomers in its lineup: UTRGV transfer Jorge Sampedro and freshman Adam Fahey .

Swimming and diving earned a split against SMU in a home meet over the weekend.

The Wildcats women won 211-89 while the men lost 155-144.

Kelsey Wasikowski led the women with a pair of individual wins in the 100 yard breast and 200 yard breast. She was also part of a first-place relay in the 200 yard medley relay.

Tomas Lukminas guided the men with wins in the 50 yard free and 100 yard free. He was part of the 400 yard free relay that took first place.

Arizona next competes in a four-team meet in Los Angeles on Nov. 7 between former Pac-12 rivals UCLA, USC and ASU.

The women's golf team competed at the Abilene Christian Intercollegiate last week, finishing in a tie for fifth in a crowded field.

Arizona shot 5-over par across three rounds. Champion Oregon led the field with a 28-under.

Sophomore Kinsley Ni finished second overall with a score of 9-under. Ni was the only Wildcats golfer to shoot under par.

Arizona has the rest of the year off before returning in February for the Thunderbird Intercollegiate, which will be held at Tucson Country Club.

articles.title: LeBron James Is Showing His Value Early With the Philadelphia 76ers
articles.summary: LeBron James is already making an impact with the Philadelphia 76ers, even if his first few games have not been perfect. The 41 year old superstar joined Phi...
articles.body:
LeBron James is already making an impact with the Philadelphia 76ers, even if his first few games have not been perfect. The 41 year old superstar joined Philadelphia during the offseason hoping to help the franchise compete for an NBA championship, and his early performances have shown that he can still contribute in multiple ways.

Through three regular season appearances, James is averaging 16.3 points, seven rebounds and 5.7 assists per game. Philadelphia won his first two games before suffering a 106-93 loss to the Detroit Pistons on Sunday.

Although the season is still young, James has given the 76ers reasons to be encouraged about what he can bring to their revamped roster.

James has not needed to dominate the ball to make an impact. His passing, rebounding and basketball IQ have helped Philadelphia organize its offense while building chemistry with his new teammates.

In his Philadelphia debut against the New York Knicks, James recorded 14 points, nine rebounds and seven assists in a 106-100 victory. He followed that performance with 17 points, 10 rebounds and five assists against the Cleveland Cavaliers as the 76ers rallied from a 29 point deficit to win 114-106.

Those performances demonstrated how James can influence a game without having to carry the scoring load every night.

With Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown providing additional offensive firepower, Philadelphia has several players capable of creating their own shots. James can focus on making the right reads, finding open teammates and taking advantage of defensive mismatches.

James also found himself in an unusual position against Detroit. With Joel Embiid and several other frontcourt players unavailable, Philadelphia started James at center.

He finished with 18 points and five assists, but the 76ers struggled defensively and lost their first game of the season.

James has made it clear that playing center is not something he expects to do regularly. With Embiid serving as Philadelphia's primary big man, the team needs its frontcourt depth to get healthier.

The experience nevertheless showed James' willingness to take on different responsibilities when his team needs him.

Can LeBron Help Philadelphia Win a Championship?

Philadelphia has assembled a talented roster, and James' championship experience could become one of its biggest advantages. His leadership and ability to control the pace of a game should help the 76ers as they work to develop chemistry.

There are still concerns about his shooting efficiency, workload and the team's rebounding. James also missed the victory over Milwaukee while managing a back issue, making workload management important early in the season.

Still, his first few appearances have offered encouraging signs. James does not need to be the best scorer every night to make Philadelphia better.

If he stays healthy and develops chemistry with Embiid, Maxey and Brown, James could be a major piece of the 76ers' championship pursuit.

articles.title: Oklahoma's defense faces major test against LaNorris Sellers
articles.summary: Oklahoma's defense emphasizes discipline, physicality and pocket containment to limit LaNorris Sellers' dual-threat ability.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners will take on the South Carolina Gamecocks in Norman on Saturday. The Gamecocks have one of college football's most talented quarterbacks, LaNorris Sellers.

He's completing 60.7% of his passes for 1,548 yards, 13 touchdowns and five interceptions, while rushing for 507 yards and four scores this season. He's familiar with Oklahoma's defense, as he's faced them twice in his career. In 2024, he was 16-of-24 for 175 yards and one score, and he rushed for 28 yards in the 35-9 win. In 2025, he was 17-of-25 for 124 yards and one score, while rushing for -9 yards thanks to six Oklahoma sacks in the Sooners' 26-7 win.

EDGE rusher Adepoju Adebawore said the defense knows what to expect this weekend.

"We've played him twice now," Adebawore said via SoonerScoop. "We know that he's fast, elusive, strong and can break tackles; he's a very, very impressive player. A guy that we just have to contain. We have to just put it together. As a d-line, we have to work together to contain him."

Taylor Wein echoed that statement, saying Oklahoma has to keep Sellers in the pocket.

"His feet are his weapon," Wein said via SoonerScoop. "He's got a heck of an arm, too. They're a way different offense than a year ago. So, we know that they are going to come in, juiced up and ready to go. We have to come in correct with our eyes, physicality and, like PJ said, containing the quarterback in the pocket and eliminating his feet."

Oklahoma's defensive front will need to be disciplined from the opening snap, particularly when Sellers escapes the pocket and looks for opportunities to extend plays. The Sooners have already shown they can pressure him, but replicating that success will require coordinated rush lanes and sound tackling. If defenders lose their assignments while chasing a sack, Sellers has the spped and strength to turn a broken play into a major gain.

articles.title: Scotland sweep aside Danes in European Championship opener
articles.summary: Scotland women begin their bid for European Curling Championship glory with a comprehensive 12-3 victory over Denmark.
articles.body:
Scotland women began their bid for European Curling Championship glory with a comprehensive 12-3 victory over Denmark.

Fay Henderson's rink edged the opening two ends by single points before the Danes halved the deficit.

However, the Scots took control of their opening match in Ostrava, surging into a five-point lead by the end of the fourth end.

Although Denmark scored two points in the fifth, Scotland ended the contest emphatically with a six-point haul in the sixth and final end.

Henderson's rink return to action on Thursday when they face Sweden, while Scotland men, led by Grant Hardie, begin their campaign against the Netherlands on Wednesday (07:30 GMT) - both matches are available to watch live on the BBC.

articles.title: Gronk Says 49ers Beat Themselves More Than Falcons Won
articles.summary: Rob Gronkowski breaks down the 49ers loss to Atlanta, citing years of injury struggles and self-inflicted errors that cost the game on Sunday.
articles.body:
Rob Gronkowski believes the San Francisco 49ers lost to the Atlanta Falcons because they failed themselves, not because Atlanta played a perfect game. The former tight end pointed to a long history of injuries plaguing the 49ers roster before Sunday's 29-20 loss at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. He argues that the team's magic will return once healthy players like Mike Evans come back after the bye week.

The 49ers dropped their first game of the season on Sunday, October 25. They now sit at 6-1 overall but face a critical injury list. According to Heavy.com , Gronkowski voiced serious worry regarding the injury bug still affecting the squad. He remains a firm believer that these issues will not affect the team in the long run.

Gronkowski asked a blunt question during his podcast. "Why are the 49ers always injured? We're not even talking about this year, not last year, I'm talking about the last 4-5 years. Why are they always injured?" He noted that many guys are on injured reserve but designated to return. The panic meter for the San Francisco 49ers is not going off according to him.

On Monday, roughly 24 hours following the defeat, head coach Kyle Shanahan addressed the media. Shanahan disclosed that seven players stand a strong likelihood of returning after the bye week. Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson are among those included in that group. Nick Bosa, the star pass rusher, is expected to return after missing the last few weeks.

The core of the loss was not a lack of talent from Atlanta. Gronkowski further stated that magic will diminish somewhat if weapons around you are absent. He thinks the magic will return immediately once Mike Evans and company resume play after the bye week. His final take on the game was sharp and direct.

"The 49ers beat themselves more than the Atlanta Falcons won this game." This statement cuts through the noise of the final score. Brock Purdy, who is currently playing at an MVP level, functions as a huddle extension of Kyle Shanahan per Gronk. The system works when the personnel is healthy. The Falcons just capitalized on the mistakes San Francisco made.

The Falcons are now 4 spots higher in power rankings according to reports. They sit at No. 21 after the upset win. This team faces its true challenge on the defensive side. Jeff Ulbrich's unit sits fourth against the run yet ranks only 29th against the pass. Converting high pressure numbers into sacks is the key to the next game.

In Week 9, James Pearce will become eligible to return from suspension which will help the pass rush. The Falcons must keep Penix upright to beat them. The 49ers loss proves that even the best teams can fall if they hurt themselves first.

articles.title: Trey Nyoni On Liverpool Chances as Iraola Embraces Youth and Rotation
articles.summary: The 19-year-old midfielder is on pace to play between 1,500 and 2,000 first team minutes this eason.
articles.body:
With Liverpool heading into the 2026-27 season without making any signings to address their depth issues in midfield, the chances were always high that 19-year-old academy graduate Trey Nyoni would be given chances to show what he could do by new head coach Andoni Iraola.

It might even be fair to say Liverpool's hopes for the season reseted in part on Nyoni being able to take those chances when they did come.

To his credit, and rather fortunately for the team, he's done just that. The youngster has made nine appearances to date, seeing the pitch in 75% of the games played in all competitions and earning 373 minutes—numbers which would project to 1,500-2,000 minutes across the entire season.

"My motive has always just been,whet her I'm on the pitch for a minute, five minutes, 10 minutes, 90 minutes, I just try to make the most out of the minutes I get," Nyoni said ahead of Wednesday's League Cup tie against Chelsea, which he is widely expected to start.

"But I think in the last few weeks obviously I've had a lot of exposure, which has been good for me. It's something different, playing a lot of minutes within a short space of tim, but it has been really good."

He's not the only youngster seeing big minutes early as Iraola looks to navigate a season where the Red will be trying to go deep and compete for silverware in four competitions despite a squad largely seen as thin at multiple positions and not just in midfield, with Rio Ngumoha and Lewis Koumas also seeing plenty of action.

"For me it's positive to see the younger players," Nyoni added. "Obviously we need to stick together, help each other as much as possible. We know that being here, it's not easy, there's a lot of world-class players here. They're going to push us every day.

"I think having that allows us to keep pushing on and keep progressing. Every time we go on the pitch, I think none of us are really nervous—I think we all go out there and give 100%. That's what's important."

articles.title: Fenerbahçe coach quits a month after previous resignation
articles.summary: Fenerbahçe coach Ismail Kartal has resigned less than 24 hours after the Istanbul derby defeat against Galatasaray. "After talks with our club leadership, th...
articles.body:
Fenerbahçe coach Ismail Kartal has resigned less than 24 hours after the Istanbul derby defeat against Galatasaray.

"After talks with our club leadership, this decision was accepted by mutual agreement and with mutual recognition and appreciation," Fenerbahçe said in a statement on Tuesday after the 2-1 league defeat. Fener are fifth, six points behind leaders Galatasaray.

In September, Kartal also offered his resignation but Fenerbahçe president Aziz Yildirim rejected it.

According to Yildirim, Kartal was then upset by a fan throwing a bottle at his head.

His fourth spell as coach at Fener ends after only a few months. He had previously managed the club in 2014-2015, 2022 and 2023-2024.

The derby between arch-rivals Galatasaray and Fenerbahçe on Monday was overshadowed by a fracas after the final whistle. Players from both teams went at each other on the pitch. Police and security forces had to intervene.

articles.title: Arsenal cup match at Fleetwood Town paused due to drone
articles.summary: A flying object caused a stoppage of just less than 10 minutes during the Gunners' visit to Fleetwood Town.
articles.body:
Arsenal's Carabao Cup match with Fleetwood Town was only two minutes old when referee Michael Salisbury stopped the match because of a drone hovering above the field.

The delay lasted less than 10 minutes as Salisbury spoke with both teams' coaching staffs, police and organizers at the intimate Highbury Stadium in northwest England.

Both teams kept warm for five minutes by staying on the field and passing a ball around before the referee called over the captains in the 8th minute and explained why he was pulling the teams off the field.

The source of the drone looked to be identified, and play resumed in the 10th minute with a free kick where an Arsenal player had been fouled eight minutes earlier.

Even before the stoppage, there were some confusing moments at the start of the game. Fleetwood Town play in red shirts with white sleeves and at a venue called Highbury, matching Arsenal's typical kit and the name of their former venue.

Fleetwood Town's Highbury, however, holds just 5,327 fans, with around 2,600 of those seated. The League Two club scored the opener thanks to 20-year-old Aaron Loupalo-Bi.

articles.title: Former Washington Nationals GM Mike Rizzo getting interviewed by the Astros
articles.summary: The long time Nationals GM is interviewing with the club he beat in the 2019 World Series
articles.body:
When he was fired in July of 2025, I was curious to see what was next for Mike Rizzo. At the time, he was 64 years old, but he did not seem to have any desire to step away. After a year on the sidelines, Rizzo is in the mix for the Astros GM job. Yesterday, Bob Nightengale reported that Rizzo would get an interview.

We will see if he gets the job, but I would sure be curious to see how he would do in Houston. The Nats and Astros also have quite a few connections. Obviously, Houston was the team that Mike Rizzo's Nats beat in the 2019 World Series. The two clubs also share a Spring Training site at West Palm Beach.

If Rizzo gets hired, we will be seeing a lot of him during Spring Training. It would be very interesting to contrast how the two teams do things at the same Spring Training site. Rizzo's successor in DC, Paul Toboni, has changed a lot since he took over. The "I don't care how hard you throw ball four" signs have been replaced by Traject Machines and other tech.

Despite Rizzo being an old school guy, I do not think it would be impossible for him to have success in Houston. He would have to adapt some, but a veteran Astros team that is not afraid to spend money would suit Rizzo better than a young, smaller budget club.

Rizzo may not be an innovator at this stage of his career, he still has an eye for a good trade and does a solid job with pro scouting. I still believe that he will have to lean into analytics more than he did, but maybe he has learned some lessons since being let go in DC. That is definitely something that will be brought up in his interview which is taking place today.

Based on his past achievements, Rizzo would be a strong candidate. He turned the Nats into one of the best teams in baseball last decade. However, the 2020's have been a different story for Rizzo. Bad drafting and an inability to adapt led to him losing his edge.

How much of this was his fault and how much was he hamstrung by the Lerner's? If he gets the Astros job, we will be able to find out. He built a World Series championship team and won the NL East four times, but there is not a ton of recent success here.

It is also no lock that Rizzo gets the job either. He is one of several candidates in the Astros search. However, the interest he is getting for this job seems to be more serious than when he was floated as a candidate for the A's gig.

If Rizzo gets the job, I will be rooting for him. Things did not end well in DC, but I appreciate the good times as well. For Astros fans sake, I hope you are getting 2010's Rizzo and not the 2020's version.

articles.title: Deion Sanders says offer of $50,000 to critics was "a joke"
articles.summary: Colorado coach Deion Sanders has addressed the comments made recently by Christopher "Uncle" Neely regarding a supposed willingness to pay critics $50,000 to...
articles.body:
Colorado coach Deion Sanders has addressed the comments made recently by Christopher "Uncle" Neely regarding a supposed willingness to pay critics $50,000 to not mention his name.

At a press conference on Tuesday, Sanders said it was " a joke ."

"I think you misinterpreted that," Sanders said. "I said . . . I would love to give you money and not mention my name, and I want to see how far that goes. That was a joke, That's what we were saying. Like some people live on your name."

Before Sanders answered, someone off camera (presumably Neely) can be heard explaining the question. The person refers to a show from the spring in which that statement was made.

Sanders did indeed previously make a comment along those lines. And it does indeed sound like a hypothetical, not an actual offer.

Separately, Deion posted the following on Twitter this afternoon: " This is a lie but God bless u all. Y'all know me and have known me for years. When has it appeared that I've EVER cared what a man or woman has said about me? My son does my Videos and Neely is a friend."

While it does appear that Sanders was not making a real offer when he talked about it previously, that's not how Neely's recent comments came off: "For the most part, the people that attack him wouldn't be making the money they were making if he wasn't here to attack. Which is why he told some of them , 'Hey man, let's just do this. I give you $50,000 to not mention my name for a year.' And ain't nobody took the deal yet. . . . And you love talking about this man so much, and you make so much talking of this man that you turned the deal down."

To answer the question Deion posed on Twitter ("When has it appeared that I've EVER cared what a man or woman has said about me?"), there is at least one tangible example of sensitivity to criticism. In 2024, for example, he refused to answer a question at a press conference from a reporter at the local CBS affiliate because of a problem he had with CBS generally.

" I'm not doing anything with CBS ," Sanders said at the time. "Next question. . . . It ain't got nothing to do with you. It's above that. It ain't got nothing to do with you. I've got love for you. I appreciate and respect you. It ain't got nothing to do with you. They know what they did."

"I'm here in Denver not national," the reporter responded.

"You are who you are," Deion replied. "CBS is CBS, all right? . . . I'm looking you in the eye as a man. I respect you. I've got love for you. But what they did was foul."

Regardless, Neely stated the offer — and the failure of any reporters to accept it — as if it were a real offer. Sanders has now given his side of the story that Neely created with the content and tone of his recent remarks.

articles.title: Nick Sirianni defended decision to play Saquon Barkley after RB suffered another injury
articles.summary: It hasn't been a great couple weeks on the injury front for the Eagles.
articles.body:
The past couple weeks haven't exactly been a banner display for the Eagles on the injury front . And on Monday, head coach Nick Sirianni once again found himself answering for the decisions of his medical team.

Eagles running back Saquon Barkley had missed the past two weeks with a hamstring injury and was listed as questionable heading into Monday night's game against the Cowboys. But after just seven carries and two receptions, Barkley exited the game and didn't return.

Though Barkley left with an announced back injury, Sirianni was still asked if he felt the Eagles rushed the star running back to return.

He defended how the Eagles handled the injury to reporters after the game. Via Pro Football Talk :

"Obviously, you saw that he was on a pitch count out there today. There was constant communication to see how he was feeling, see where he was, and obviously, he came out early in the second half. Again, when you go into something like that, you make sure that the player's health is first and foremost. Is he ready to go? Do they feel ready to go? Do the doctors and trainers feel like they're ready to go? We felt like that was the case today, but obviously wanted to keep a close eye on him, and he's tough as heck. He wanted to be out there for his teammates, probably had to slow him [down] as far as -- he'd be out there every play because of the person he is and the teammate he is and the player he is and the toughness that he has. "So, we tried to be smart with him there, but it was good to have him back out there. He obviously had a nice game and was very productive when he touched the football."

articles.summary: SALT LAKE CITY (AP) — Jazz forward Jaren Jackson Jr. will be sidelined for at least six weeks after tearing the MCL in his right knee during the second quart...
articles.body:
SALT LAKE CITY (AP) — Jazz forward Jaren Jackson Jr. will be sidelined for at least six weeks after tearing the MCL in his right knee during the second quarter of Utah's 110-105 loss to the Memphis Grizzlies .

Lauri Markkanen, who sprained his right wrist in the first quarter of the same game on Monday night, is listed as day to day.

Jackson and Markkanen were two of the top three scorers for the Jazz in the team's first three games.

Both players have struggled with injuries during their time in Utah.

Markkanen appeared in only 89 games over his previous two seasons with the Jazz and has not appeared in more than 66 games in a season since being traded to Utah before the 2022-23 season.

Jackson only appeared in three games with Utah last season after being acquired in a trade with Memphis before undergoing season-ending surgery on his left knee.

articles.title: Hail State star QB Kamario Taylor to miss Longhorns game, season
articles.summary: The Longhorns will not face Kamario Taylor on Saturday. The star Mississippi State QB has been ruled out for the rest of the season.
articles.body:
One of college football's breakout stars is out for the season and will miss Saturday's clash in Austin to take on the Texas Longhorns . Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor will miss the rest of the season after it was announced he'd need surgery on his injured toe.

Taylor injured his toe on Sept. 26 against Missouri. He has tried to play in two games since, against Alabama on Oct. 3 and Oklahoma this past Saturday. In both efforts, the Macon, MS product didn't look anywhere close to 100% and left both games early. In fact, it looked like he made it worse against the Sooners.

The true sophomore entered the national spotlight after leading Hail State to a 4-0 record. The Bulldogs have struggled to win any games over the past few seasons. Taylor was under center for wins against Minnesota and South Carolina on the road and No. 19 Missouri at home.

Taylor's season ends with 17 passing touchdowns, 1,460 passing yards and a 65% completion percentage. At 6-foot-4 and 230 pounds, he is physically a lot like Vince Young and is already one of the country's most dominant and dangerous players.

articles.title: Maryland football hires search firm to help with finding new HC after Mike Locksley firing
articles.summary: As the Maryland football team fired head coach Mike Locksley after another disappointing season, the program is making efforts to find the next best option f...
articles.body:
As the Maryland football team fired head coach Mike Locksley after another disappointing season, the program is making efforts to find the next best option for the school. While rumors surround the Maryland football team regarding the next head coach, the latest development details the next step in finding the next head coach.

According to college football insider Pete Nakos of On3 Sports, the Terrapins have hired "search firm ZRG Turnkey" to help with the search for the school's future head coach after Locksley.

"Maryland has hired search firm ZRG Turnkey to assist with its head football coaching search, sources tell [On3]," Nakos wrote Tuesday on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Athletic director Jim Smith spoke about the decision, saying that the school "will get a really good coach," according to The Baltimore Sun.

"I was fortunate enough to [have] the bye week," Smith said. "So there wasn't the immediate urgency. There aren't also a lot of bye week changes. As you saw this week, there were two coaches let go, and it was immediate. So I had a little bit more time. I wanted to make sure I was not making an emotional decision, and we came to the right conclusion for the program when we announced on Wednesday."

The news of Maryland football firing Mike Locksley was a "stunner"

When it comes to the players' reactions to the news, outside linebacker Sidney Stewart would be honest in saying how much of a "stunner" it was to see Locksley fired.

"For it to actually happen, it definitely was a stunner for me and the rest of the team," Stewart said. "I have a lot of love for him. I really appreciate him. He's impacted me on and off the field. But ultimately, I know that the people that are still here and are part of this program made the right choice…so I'm just riding the ship."

Locksley has coached the Terrapins since 2019, amassing a 39-54 record with the program. With Aazaar Abdul-Rahim as the interim head coach, he'll look to lead Maryland (2-5) on Saturday against Illinois, hoping to snap the five-game skid.
